verses.zh: 大卫年纪老迈，日子满足，就立他儿子所罗门作以色列的王。
verses.en: When David was old and approaching the end of his life,[NOTE:1] he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
notes: Heb “and full of years.”

verses.zh: 大卫招聚以色列的众首领和祭司利未人。
verses.en: David[NOTE:1] assembled all the leaders of Israel, along with the priests and the Levites.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 利未人从三十岁以外的都被数点，他们男丁的数目共有三万八千；
verses.en: The Levites who were thirty years old and up were counted; there were 38,000 men.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and their number by their heads, by men, was 38,000.”

verses.zh: 其中有二万四千人管理耶和华殿的事，有六千人作官长和士师，
verses.en: David said,[NOTE:1] “Of these, 24,000 are to direct the work of the Lord’s temple; 6,000 are to be officials and judges;
notes: The words “David said” are supplied here in the translation for clarification. The appearance of the first person verb “I supplied” in v. 5 indicates that David is speaking here.

verses.zh: 有四千人作守门的，又有四千人用大卫所做的乐器颂赞耶和华。
verses.en: 4,000 are to be gatekeepers; and 4,000 are to praise the Lord with the instruments I supplied for worship.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “made to [or “for”] praise.”

verses.zh: 大卫将利未人革顺、哥辖、米拉利的子孙分了班次。
verses.en: David divided them into groups corresponding to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

verses.zh: 革顺的子孙有拉但和示每。
verses.en: The Gershonites included Ladan and Shimei.

verses.zh: 拉但的长子是耶歇，还有细坦和约珥，共三人。
verses.en: The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the oldest, Zetham, and Joel—three in all.

verses.zh: 示每的儿子是示罗密、哈薛、哈兰三人。这是拉但族的族长。
verses.en: The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran—three in all.These were the leaders of the family of Ladan.

verses.zh: 示每的儿子是雅哈、细拿、耶乌施、比利亚共四人。
verses.en: The sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina,[NOTE:1] Jeush, and Beriah. These were Shimei’s sons—four in all.[NOTE:2]
notes: The MT reads “Zina” here and “Zizah” in v. 11. One Hebrew ms, the LXX, and the Vulgate, harmonizing the form of the name to that found in v. 11, read “Zizah” here.

Verses 8-10 are confusing. Two different lists of Shimei’s sons appear. In between these lists is the statement “these were the leaders of the family of Ladan,” suggesting that the list just before this includes the sons of Ladan, not Shimei. But verse 8 already lists Ladan’s sons. Apparently the text as it stands is a conflation of differing traditions.

verses.zh: 雅哈是长子，细撒是次子。但耶乌施和比利亚的子孙不多，所以算为一族。
verses.en: Jahath was the oldest and Zizah the second oldest. Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they were considered one family with one responsibility.

verses.zh: 哥辖的儿子是暗兰、以斯哈、希伯伦、乌薛共四人。
verses.en: The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel—four in all.

verses.zh: 暗兰的儿子是亚伦、摩西。亚伦和他的子孙分出来，好分别至圣的物，在耶和华面前烧香、事奉他，奉他的名祝福，直到永远。
verses.en: The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses.Aaron and his descendants were chosen on a permanent basis to consecrate the most holy items, to offer sacrifices before the Lord, to serve him, and to praise his name.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and Aaron was set apart to consecrate it, the most holy things, he and his sons, permanently, to sacrifice before the Lord, to serve him, and to bless his name permanently.”

verses.zh: 至于神人摩西，他的子孙名字记在利未支派的册上。
verses.en: The descendants of Moses the man of God were considered Levites.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and Moses the man of God, his sons were called to the tribe of Levi.”

verses.zh: 摩西的儿子是革舜和以利以谢。
verses.en: The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.

verses.zh: 革舜的长子是细布业；
verses.en: The son[NOTE:1] of Gershom: Shebuel[NOTE:2] the oldest.
notes: The Hebrew text has the plural “sons,” but only one name appears after this. The attached phrase “the oldest” might indicate that Shebuel was not Gershom’s only son, but note v. 17.
The LXX reads Σουβαηλ (Soubaēl) here, a reading followed by NAB, NIV, NCV, CEV (“Shubael”); cf. 24:20.

verses.zh: 以利以谢的儿子是利哈比雅。以利以谢没有别的儿子，但利哈比雅的子孙甚多。
verses.en: The son of Eliezer was[NOTE:1] Rehabiah, the oldest. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah had many descendants.
notes: The Hebrew text has “the sons of Eliezer were,” but only one name appears after this in the verse, and we are specifically told that Eliezer had no other sons.

verses.zh: 以斯哈的长子是示罗密。
verses.en: The son[NOTE:1] of Izhar: Shelomith the oldest.
notes: The Hebrew text has the plural “sons,” but only one name appears after this. The attached phrase “the oldest” might indicate that Shelomith was not Izhar’s only son, but note v. 17.

verses.zh: 希伯伦的长子是耶利雅，次子是亚玛利亚，三子是雅哈悉，四子是耶加面。
verses.en: The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the oldest, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.

verses.zh: 乌薛的长子是米迦，次子是耶西雅。
verses.en: The sons of Uzziel: Micah the oldest, and Isshiah the second.

verses.zh: 米拉利的儿子是抹利、母示。抹利的儿子是以利亚撒、基士。
verses.en: The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi.The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.

verses.zh: 以利亚撒死了，没有儿子，只有女儿，他们本族基士的儿子娶了她们为妻。
verses.en: Eleazar died without having sons; he had only daughters. The sons of Kish, their cousins, married them.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the sons of Kish, their brothers [i.e., relatives/cousins] lifted them up.” For other uses of נָאָשׂ (naʾas, “lift up”) in the sense of “marry,” see BDB 671 s.v. Qal.3.d.

verses.zh: 母示的儿子是末力、以得、耶利摩共三人。
verses.en: The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth—three in all.

verses.zh: 以上利未子孙作族长的，照着男丁的数目，从二十岁以外，都办耶和华殿的事务。
verses.en: These were the descendants of Levi according to their families, that is, the leaders of families as counted and individually listed who carried out assigned tasks in the Lord’s temple and were twenty years old and up.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “these were the sons of Levi according to the house of their fathers, heads of the fathers, according to their numberings, by number of names, according to their heads, doer[s] of the work for the service of the house of the Lord, from a son of twenty years and upwards.”

verses.zh: 大卫说：「耶和华―以色列的　神已经使他的百姓平安，他永远住在耶路撒冷。
verses.en: For David said, “The Lord God of Israel has given his people rest and has permanently settled in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 利未人不必再抬帐幕和其中所用的一切器皿了。」
verses.en: So the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the items used in its service.”

verses.zh: 照着大卫临终所吩咐的，利未人从二十岁以外的都被数点。
verses.en: According to David’s final instructions, the Levites twenty years old or older were counted.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for by the final words of David, they were the number of the sons of Levi, from a son of twenty years and upward.”

verses.zh: 他们的职任是服事亚伦的子孙，在耶和华的殿和院子，并屋中办事，洁净一切圣物，就是办　神殿的事务，
verses.en: Their job was to help Aaron’s descendants in the service of the Lord’s temple. They were to take care of the courtyards, the rooms, ceremonial purification of all holy items, and other jobs related to the service of God’s temple.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “For their assignment was at the hand of the sons of Aaron for the work of the house of the Lord concerning the courtyards and concerning the rooms and concerning the purification of all holiness and the work of the service of the house of God.”

verses.zh: 并管理陈设饼，素祭的细面，或无酵薄饼，或用盘烤，或用油调和的物，又管理各样的升斗尺度；
verses.en: They also took care of[NOTE:1] the bread that is displayed, the flour for offerings, the unleavened wafers, the round cakes, the mixing, and all the measuring.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “with respect to.”
The Hebrew terms מְשׂוּרָה (mesurah) and מִדָּה (middah) refer to different types of measurements.

verses.zh: 每日早晚，站立称谢赞美耶和华，
verses.en: They also stood in a designated place[NOTE:1] every morning and offered thanks and praise to the Lord. They also did this in the evening
notes: Heb “and to stand.”

verses.zh: 又在安息日、月朔，并节期，按数照例，将燔祭常常献给耶和华；
verses.en: and whenever burnt sacrifices were offered to the Lord on the Sabbath and at new moon festivals and assemblies. A designated number were to serve before the Lord regularly in accordance with regulations.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “by number according to the manner upon them, regularly before the Lord.”

verses.zh: 又看守会幕和圣所，并守耶和华吩咐他们弟兄亚伦子孙的，办耶和华殿的事。
verses.en: They were in charge of the meeting tent and the Holy Place, and helped their relatives, the descendants of Aaron, in the service of the Lord’s temple.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and they kept the charge of the tent of meeting and the charge of the holy place and the charge of the sons of Aaron, their brothers, for the service of the house of the Lord.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- David was concerned with Solomon's leadership and administration because of his youth, so he
provided the building materials. He also organized the temple servants (as Moses had done).

- The Chronicler emphasizes David's role in Solomon's temple and its personnel and procedures in order to emphasize
the rebuilt, second temple of his day. It was small but it was a continuation of God's guidelines to Moses as developed
by the ideal king, David.

- 1 Chronicles 23:1-27:34 is a literary unit dealing with David's organization of temple personnel
and procedures. It seems 1 Chr. 23:2 links to 28:1.

- Ezra and Nehemiah document the early post-exilic period, while the Chronicler documents the
later development. See Introduction, Date. Much of the difference between

- Moses

- David

- Ezra (chapter 2) ‒ Nehemiah (chapter 7)

- Ezra (chapter 2) ‒ Nehemiah (chapter 7)
is simply the development of procedures due to changing conditions.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 23:1-2

1Now when David reached old age, he made his son Solomon king over Israel. 2And he gathered
together all the leaders of Israel with the priests and the Levites.

23:1 "reached old age" This is literally "became old and sated with days." This is an idiom (cf. 2 Chr. 24:15) for a
long life. It was not an emphasis of satisfaction with one's life but the length of one's life.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HUMAN AGING

▣ "he made his son Solomon king" From 1 Chr. 28:5 we know it was YHWH's choice, not David's.
Solomon's succession is mentioned several times.

- 1 Chr. 22:5,6,9,10

- 1 Chr. 28:5-8

- 1 Chr. 29:1-30

All of the problems associated with Solomon found in 1 Kings 1-2 are omitted.

23:2 "all the leaders" See note at 1 Chr. 22:17. One wonders how this verse relates to 1 Chr. 28:1. If they
are the same, then 1 Chr. 23:3-27:34 is an insertion.

For a good brief discussion of "Levites" see NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 772-777.

▣ "the priests and Levites" All the servants at the temple were descendants of Aaron (except the Nethilim,
Ezra 2:43,58,70; 7:7; 8:17,20). Some of his sons became priests who offered sacrifices and some took care of the
tabernacle/temple. The Levites' specific duties, now that the ark's location is permanent (cf. 1 Chr. 23:25-26) have changed
and are listed in 1 Chr. 23:28-31.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVITICAL
PRIESTS

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 23:3-6

3The Levites were numbered from thirty years old and upward, and their number by census of men was 38,000.
4Of these, 24,000 were to oversee the work of the house of the Lord; and 6,000
were officers and judges, 5and 4,000 were gatekeepers, and 4,000 were praising the
Lord with the instruments which David made for giving praise. 6David divided them
into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

23:3 It is specifically mentioned that Joab did not count the Levites (cf. 1 Chr. 21:6). Here, they are counted
but with no negative remarks. Possibly because this census was for the organization of the temple, not David's military.

23:4-5 There are several kinds of Levites.

- those who oversee the work of the house of the Lord

- officers ‒ BDB 1009 (cf. 1 Chr. 26:29; 2 Chr. 19:11; 34:13)

- judges ‒ BDB 1047; there were religious and non-religious judges, cf. Deut. 17:9,12; 19:17

- gatekeepers ‒ BDB 1045; 1 Chr. 15:18; 16:38; 26:13; 2 Chr. 8:14; Ezra 2:42,70; 7:7; Neh. 7:1, 45, 73

- musicians ‒ cf. 1 Chr. 15:16; 16:4-5,42; 25:1-8 (but the priests blew the trumpets, cf. 2 Chr. 29:26)

Since the Levites now helped with the temple, they must be supported by offerings to the temple
(cf. Neh. 10:39; 12:47; 13:5,10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TITHES IN THE MOSAIC LEGISLATION

23:4

NASB, Peshitta
"to oversee the work"

NKJV
"to look after the work"

NRSV
"have charge of the work"

TEV
"administer the work"

NJB
"responsible for the service"

JPSOA
"in charge of the work"

REB
"responsible for the maintenance"

LXX
"taskmasters over the tasks"

This VERB (BDB 663 I, KB 716, Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)
has several connotations.

- supervising the building of the temple ‒ 2 Chr. 2:2,18; 34:12,13; Ezra 3:8,9

- maintaining the ministry/service of the temple ‒ 1 Chr. 23:4,32

- conducting the liturgical and musical aspects of worship ‒ 1 Chr. 15:21 and the title "choir director," which appears in
many of the MT's Introduction in the Psalms (i.e., Psalm 4; 5; 6; 8; etc.)

In this context #3 fits best.

23:6 This lists the sons of Levi.

- Gershon ‒ see 1 Chr. 23:7-12; Num. 4:21-28

- Kohath ‒ see 1 Chr. 23:12-20; Num. 4:4-15 (family of Aaron and Moses, 1 Chr. 23:13)

- Merari ‒ see 1 Chr. 23:21-23; Num. 4:29-33

This follows Exod. 6:16-19; Num. 3:14-20; and 1 Chr. 6:16-30.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 23:7-11

7Of the Gershonites were Ladan and Shimei. 8The sons of Ladan were Jehiel the
first and Zetham and Joel, three. 9The sons of Shimei were Shelomoth and Haziel and Haran, three.
These were the heads of the fathers' households of Ladan. 10The sons of Shimei were Jahath,
Zina, Jeush and Beriah. These four were the sons of Shimei. 11Jahath was the first and Zizah the second;
but Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they became a father's household, one class.

23:7 "Ladan" In Exod. 6:17 his name is spelled "Libni."

23:10 "Zina" In the next verse it is spelled "Zizah." The Chronicler is obviously using different lists.

- Notice that there are two lists of the sons of Shimei; 1 Chr. 23:9 and 10 differ.

- The name of Eliezer's son is spelled differently between 1 Chr. 23:17a and 17b.

- 1 Chr. 23:16 has "sons" but lists only one called "the first."

- The same as 1 Chr. 23:16, 23:17 has "sons" but only one named, called "the first."

- Same for 1 Chr. 23:18.

- The list of 1 Chr. 23:16-23 is repeated with variations in 24:26-30.

- The age of Levites in 1 Chr. 23:3 is changed in 23:27.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 23:12-20

12The sons of Kohath were four: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel. 13The sons of Amram were
Aaron and Moses. And Aaron was set apart to sanctify him as most holy, he and his sons forever, to burn incense before the
Lord, to minister to Him and to bless in His name forever. 14But as for Moses
the man of God, his sons were named among the tribe of Levi. 15The sons of Moses were Gershom and
Eliezer. 16The son of Gershom was Shebuel the chief. 17The son of Eliezer was Rehabiah the
chief; and Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very many. 18The son of Izhar was
Shelomith the chief. 19The sons of Hebron were Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third and
Jekameam the fourth. 20The sons of Uzziel were Micah the first and Isshiah the second.

23:13 The duties of the priests were:

- to burn incense before the Lord

- to minister to Him

- to bless His name

▣ "Aaron. . .most holy. . .and his sons" This designation (BDB 871 CONSTRUCT BDB 871)
is a play on the word "sanctify" (BDB 872). It was used to show the higher status of priests over Levites, who are only
designated as "holy" (cf. 2 Chr. 23:60.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

23:16 "Shebuel" In 1 Chr. 24:20 he is called "Shubael."

23:18 "Shelomith" In 1 Chr. 24:22 he is called "Shelomoth."

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 23:21-23

21The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli were Eleazar and Kish.
22Eleazar died and had no sons, but daughters only, so their brothers, the sons of Kish, took
them as wives. 23The sons of Mushi were three: Mahli, Eder and Jeremoth.

23:22 Tribal identification was significant because of the Divine allotment of land by Joshua (cf. Joshua 12-
19). A similar procedure is documented in Num. 27:1-8; 36:1-9.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 23:24-32

24These were the sons of Levi according to their fathers' households, even the heads of the fathers'
households of those of them who were counted, in the number of names by their census, doing the work for the
service of the house of the Lord, from twenty years old and upward. 25For David
said, "The Lord God of Israel has given rest to His people, and He dwells in Jerusalem forever.
26Also, the Levites will no longer need to carry the tabernacle and all its utensils for its service." 27For
by the last words of David the sons of Levi were numbered from twenty years old and upward. 28For
their office is to assist the sons of Aaron with the service of the house of the Lord, in the courts
and in the chambers and in the purifying of all holy things, even the work of the service of the house of God, 29and
with the showbread, and the fine flour for a grain offering, and unleavened wafers, or what is baked in the pan or what is
well-mixed, and all measures of volume and size. 30They are to stand every morning to thank and to praise the
Lord, and likewise at evening, 31and to offer all burnt offerings to the
Lord, on the sabbaths, the new moons and the fixed festivals in the number set by the ordinance
concerning them, continually before the Lord. 32Thus they are to keep charge of
the tent of meeting, and charge of the holy place, and charge of the sons of Aaron their relatives, for the service of the house
of the Lord.

23:25 This verse alludes to 1 Chr. 22:18. "Rest" was a way of denoting that the full extent of the Promised Land
was occupied and without rebellion or foreign conflict.

▣ "He dwells in Jerusalem" This is referring to YHWH dwelling above the Mercy Seat on the ark between the
wings of the Cherubim.

Jerusalem was the final site for the worship of YHWH. This special choice by YHWH (i.e., "the place
I cause My name to dwell") is repeated often in Deuteronomy.

The ark and the tent were originally together

- in the wilderness and Moab

- Gilgal ‒ Jos. 4:15-5:12

- Shiloh ‒ Jos. 18:1; 19:51; 1 Sam. 2:22

- Gibeon ‒ 1 Chr. 16:39-40; 2 Chr. 1:3-6

- now Jerusalem ‒ 1 Chr. 23:25

SPECIAL TOPIC: MERCY SEAT

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHERUBIM

▣ "forever" This word must be interpreted in context.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO OT COVENANT PROMISES SEEM SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

23:27 The age differs in 1 Chr. 23:3. This same thing is seen in Num. 4:3 compared to Num. 8:24. As more
and more Levites were needed, the bottom age was lowered.

- 30-50 years

- 25-50 years

- here, 20-50 years

Fifty was always the top age.

23:28-31 The Levites are to assist the priests

- by working in the courts and chambers

- in purifying all holy things

- in making showbread

- in producing the fine flour of the grain offering

- in making unleavened wafers

- in making all baked goods

- by being involved daily in blessing rituals

- by being involved in the sacrifices (both at festivals and each day [i.e., washing the animals; clearing the ashes; etc.])

- in helping administer the temple and the priests

- later they became local teachers (cf. 2 Chr. 17:8; 35:3; Neh. 8:7-8)

This would develop into rabbinical Judaism's position of "rabbi" (i.e., "teacher"). Ezra was the first of this
category.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHOW BREAD or BREAD OF THE PRESENCE

23:29 "all measures of volume and size" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANCIENT NEAR EASTERN WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES; also note Lev. 19:25.

23:30 The morning and evening sacrifice of a lamb is called "the Continual" (cf. Exod. 29:38-41; Num. 28:3-8;
1 Chr. 16:40).

▣ "thank. . .praise" These are used together to denote singing (cf. 1 Chr. 16:4; 23:30; 25:3; Ezra 3:11;
Neh. 12:24,46).

23:31 "sabbath" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH (OT).

▣ "the fixed festivals" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FEASTS OF ISRAEL.

23:32 "the holy place" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: CHART OF THE TABERNACLE.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why is the author of Chronicles emphasizing the temple and its organization?

- How are priests and Levites both the same and different?

- Were there civil judges or religious judges?

- What specific tasks are given to priests (1 Chr. 23:13) and Levites (1 Chr. 23:4-5,28-31)?

- Why was the census of the Levites not a sin? (i.e., compare 1 Chr. 21:1)?

- Why is the age of Levites entering temple service different here (1 Chr. 23:24) from 1 Chr. 23:3 and Num. 4:3 and 8:24?
